lesson.subject: numeracy
lesson.title: Area of Rectangles
lesson.subtitle: Term 4 Week 5, Session 2
lesson.footer: Area and Perimeter | Year 5/6 Maths | Session 2

plan.curriculum: Mathematics 2.0, Number, Year 5 (VC2M5N06) applied to measurement: multiplying larger numbers by one- and two-digit numbers with efficient strategies to find the area of rectangles, and checking reasonableness
plan.shape: short-cycle loops: model one strategy, try one, then the next strategy, because choosing an efficient strategy is the new skill
plan.criticalFeature: area = length x width, in square units; split or double and halve to make the multiplication easy
decisionPoints: the choice check: area of a 9 m by 7 m rectangle
the hinge: area of a 27 m by 8 m rectangle
plan.anchor: perimeter goes around the edge (add the sides); area covers the inside (length x width)
plan.catchUp: Missed Session 1? Trace the edge of a rectangle (perimeter) then shade its inside (area) before the launch.

manipulatives: Square tiles or grid paper for counting (optional)
studentTools: Printed Worksheet for every student; Extension and Supported Worksheet as needed
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
boardSetup: The week's anchor on the board: perimeter goes around the edge (add the sides); area covers the inside (length x width)
Strategy list: split the long side; double and halve; the written method

slides.notes: Session 2 of our area and perimeter week: today we find the area of rectangles.
Before you start, put boards and markers on every desk, and write the strategy list on the board. Print the Worksheet for everyone, and a few copies of the Extension and the Supported Worksheet.

slides.title: Read the graph
prompts: How many more books did Ava read than Leo?

beats: SAY: Let's warm up with graphs, angles and chance.
ASK: How many more books did Ava read than Leo?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 7
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> lay a ruler across each column top and read the scale. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Ava read 15 and Leo read 8,
so Ava read 7 more. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 15, Ava's total.
Fix: ask what 'how many more' means, and they subtract.
notes.prep: Review of Week 3 statistics (the request named the focus). Keep the review under 6 minutes.

beats: ASK: How big is the reflex angle?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 280
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> trace the full turn, then take away the inside angle. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 280 degrees, because 360 take away 80 is 280.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 100, from 180.
Fix: trace all the way round, and they redo it from 360.

slides.title: Relative frequency
prompts: A dice showed six 6 times in 40 rolls. Write the relative frequency of six as a percentage.

beats: ASK: What is the relative frequency of six, as a percentage?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 15%
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then on to Fluency.
Less -> write 6 over 40, then make it out of 100. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 6 out of 40 is 15 out of 100,
so 15 percent. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 6%.
Fix: ask what the total is, and they make it out of 100.

slides.title: Multiply with the written method: 3 digits

beats: SAY: Now for some written multiplication.
Multiply the ones first, and carry into the next column.
ASK: Use the written method to solve this one.
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 3 402
SCAN boards for the carried digits.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> model the first column together on the board, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The answer is 3 402.
Tick it or fix it, and check every step.
trap: forgetting to add the carried digit after multiplying.
Fix: write each carry small above the next column, and they redo it.
notes.prep: Multiplication fluency: 3 digits, then 4, then 5. Keep the whole block under 6 minutes.

slides.title: Multiply with the written method: 4 digits

beats: SAY: Now it's 4 digits.
It's the same method, just one more column.
ASK: Use the written method to solve this one.
45 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 24 600
SCAN boards for the carried digits.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> model the first column together on the board, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The answer is 24 600.
Tick it or fix it, and check every step.
trap: forgetting to add the carried digit after multiplying.
Fix: write each carry small above the next column, and they redo it.

slides.title: Multiply with the written method: 5 digits

beats: SAY: Now it's 5 digits.
It's the same method, just one more column.
ASK: Use the written method to solve this one.
60 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 148 098
SCAN boards for the carried digits.
80%+ -> reveal, then the learning intention.
Less -> model the first column together on the board, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The answer is 148 098.
Tick it or fix it, and check every step.
trap: forgetting to add the carried digit after multiplying.
Fix: write each carry small above the next column, and they redo it.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to find the area of rectangles using efficient multiplication.
successCriteria: I can find the area of a rectangle by counting squares or multiplying length by width.
I can multiply larger numbers to find an area, choosing an efficient strategy.
I can explain why area is measured in square units.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: Yesterday we went around the edge.
Today we find how much space is inside: the area.
SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: The first one is where we start,
and the second one is our big goal today.
notes.prep: SC1 counting and length x width is reachable for everyone; SC2 efficient multiplication is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 square units is the stretch.

slides.title: Cover it with squares
slides.prompt: How many squares cover the rectangle?

beats: POINT to the squares.
SAY: This rectangle is covered in squares. How many are there altogether?
ASK: How many squares cover the rectangle?
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 24
SCAN boards for 24.
80%+ -> cold call one student:
Did you count them all, or find a quicker way?
Less -> count one row, 6, then count the rows, 4. Re-ask.
SAY: It's 24: 4 rows of 6.
Multiplying the rows by the squares in each row is much faster than counting.
trap: counting the edge only.
Fix: say area covers the inside, and they count again.
notes.prep: The launch comes after the LI: area as covering with squares, then rows times columns. Under 4 minutes.

slides.meaning: The amount of surface a shape covers, measured in square units.
slides.example: A 5 m by 3 m rug covers 15 square metres, written 15 m².

beats: POINT to the word.
SAY: This word is area. Say it with me: ar-e-a.
SAY: Area is how much surface a shape covers.
We measure it in squares, like square metres, written with a little 2: m squared.
ASK: Show me with your hands: is area the edge or the inside?
5 sec. Cue: Everyone, together, on three. Show... now.
EXPECT: hands rubbing the inside of the desk
trap: writing m instead of m².
Fix: point to the squares, and they add the little 2.
notes.prep: Square units: m² and cm². The little 2 means square.

beats: POINT to the rectangle.
SAY: This garden is 23 metres by 6 metres.
23 times 6 is tricky in my head,
so I split the long side into 20 and 3.
MODEL the two parts.
SAY: 20 times 6 is 120, and 3 times 6 is 18.
I add the two parts: 138 square metres.
ASK: Use the same split.
What is the area of a rectangle 34 metres by 5 metres?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 170 m²
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 30 times 5 is 150,
and 4 times 5 is 20, so 170 square metres.
trap: multiplying only the tens.
Fix: point to the small part of the area model, and they add it.
notes.help: Draw two boxes; write each part inside.
notes.prep: Split the long side: the area model matches the written method. SC2.

beats: POINT to 25 and 16.
SAY: Here's another strategy.
When one number is 25 or 50, doubling it makes it easy.
MODEL double and halve.
SAY: If I double 25 and halve 16,
the area stays the same: 50 times 8.
Again: 100 times 4, which is 400 square metres.
ASK: Use double and halve.
What is the area of a rectangle 15 metres by 18 metres?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 270 m²
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Double 15 is 30 and half of 18 is 9,
so 30 times 9 is 270 square metres.
trap: doubling both numbers.
Fix: say one doubles, one halves, and they redo it.
notes.stretch: Why does doubling one side and halving the other keep the area the same?
notes.help: Write each step on a new line.
notes.prep: Double one side, halve the other: the area stays the same. SC2 and SC3.

slides.title: A 9 m by 7 m rectangle
slides.prompt: What is the area? Point to A, B or C

options.misconception: finds the perimeter, not the area
adds the length and width instead of multiplying

beats: SAY: Area covers the inside. Think before you point.
ASK: What is the area of a 9 metre by 7 metre rectangle?
15 sec. Cue: Voices off. Point... now. Hold your point.
EXPECT: pointing to B
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then cold call one student: What did A find?
Less -> sketch the rectangle, then rows times squares in a row. Re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: It's B, 63 square metres: 9 times 7.
A is the perimeter, and C added instead of multiplying.
trap: pointing to A.
Fix: say area covers, perimeter goes around, and they choose again.
notes.prep: First decision point. A: perimeter confused with area; C: adding instead of multiplying.

slides.title: Find the area
slides.ask: What is the area? Choose an efficient strategy.
slides.pivot: draw the area model and split the long side
slides.followUp: cold call one board: Which strategy did you choose, and why?

items.say: Double and halve: 90 times 2 is 180 square centimetres.
25 times 4 is 100, and 32 is 8 fours, so 800.
A square: 13 times 13. Split it: 130 plus 39 is 169.

say: Write the area, with square units, on your board.
trap: forgetting the square units.
Fix: point to the little 2, and they add it.
notes.help: Draw the area model and split it.
notes.prep: Guided practice: counting, splitting, doubling and halving, then a square. SC2.

beats: SAY: This one is just for you.
Choose your strategy.
ASK: What is the area of a rectangle 27 metres by 8 metres?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 216 m²
SCAN every board, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then Your turn.
Less -> split 27 into 20 and 7 on an area model together. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 20 times 8 is 160, and 7 times 8 is 56: 216 square metres.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 70.
Fix: say area covers the inside, and they multiply.
notes.prep: The hinge before independent work. Anyone with 70 (perimeter) or a place value slip starts on the Supported Worksheet with the teacher.

slides.title: Your turn
slides.task: Find areas with efficient strategies on your worksheet.

beats: POINT to the steps.
SAY: Read each question carefully, solve it carefully, then check your answers.
SAY: If you finish, the Extension is your early finisher option.
Let's read the steps together. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE and ask: Which strategy did you choose for that one?
TIME: 20 minutes. Stop everyone once at 10 minutes to share a strategy.
trap: adding instead of multiplying.
Fix: point to the area model, and they multiply.
notes.stretch: Extension: factor strategies, same area with different perimeters, and a puzzle.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: grids to count, rows times columns, and hints.
notes.prep: Independent practice: counting, efficient multiplication and real problems. The sheet is evidence for SC2 and SC3.

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: What is the area of the basketball court?

beats: SAY: Here's the last one. Work it out on your own board.
ASK: What is the area of a basketball court 28 metres by 15 metres?
40 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 420 m²
RECORD who finds the perimeter or slips in the multiplication.
They start tomorrow's check with the teacher.
trap: writing 86.
Fix: none now. Record the name for tomorrow.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2: a two-digit by two-digit area in context.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Tell your partner the strategy you like best for area, and why.

notes.answer: open - listen for split, double and halve, or the written method, with a reason
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How sure are you that you can find the area of a rectangle?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit board.
A thumb up with 86 on the board matters most.
ASK: Which area strategy do you like best, and why?
20 sec. Cue: Partner A first. You have 20 seconds. Go.
EXPECT: split, double and halve, or the written method, with a reason
notes.prep: Read the self-assessment beside the exit evidence. Tomorrow: area problems with division.
